the chemical species of the gas with its physical state
the volume of the container holding the gas with unit
the temperature of the gas with unit
outputs: inputs are valid for the perfect gas model

inputs: the temperature of the gas with unit

inputs: the volume of the container holding the gas with unit

functions.description: Convert a pressure in pascals to atmospheres and megapascals for reporting
Cross-check a perfect gas pressure by recomputing it with the gas constant in L atm K-1 mol-1.
inputs: the amount of substance of the gas in mol
the volume of the container holding the gas with unit
outputs: agreement of the two pressure computations

functions.description: Predict the pressure exerted by a perfect gas from its amount, species, volume and temperature.
inputs: the amount of substance of the gas in mol
the chemical species of the gas with its physical state
the volume of the container holding the gas with unit
the temperature of the gas with unit
outputs: pressure of the gas in MPa
pressure of the gas in Pa
pressure of the gas in atm

entry_points.text: Suppose that ●1 ●2 is confined to ●3 at ●4. Predict the pressure exerted by the ethane from the perfect gas.

params.description: the amount of substance of the gas in mol
params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite number (n > 0). Zero moles gives zero pressure; negative or non-physical amounts are invalid. No upper bound is imposed by the equation itself, but the perfect gas result is only physically realistic when the implied pressure stays low enough for ideal behaviour.

params.description: the chemical species of the gas with its physical state
params.validity_range: Must name a substance that is a gas at the given temperature and pressure. The perfect gas law applies only in the gas phase, so the species must not condense at the stated conditions. Ethane is gaseous at 300 K, but its critical temperature (about 305 K) lies close to this temperature, so high-pressure results are approximate.

params.description: the volume of the container holding the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite volume (V > 0) with a unit convertible to m3. Zero or negative volume is physically impossible and would make the pressure undefined or negative.

params.description: the temperature of the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a thermodynamic temperature strictly above absolute zero, i.e. above 0 K or -273.15 °C. Temperatures at or below 0 K are invalid. The gas must also be above its condensation point for the gas-phase assumption to hold.
